title: Plant and Animal Cells
competency: Differentiate plant and animal cells based on their organelles and recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell while others consist of many cells.
objectives: Identify the major organelles found in plant and animal cells.
Explain the functions of the cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria, and chloroplasts.
Compare and contrast plant and animal cells.
Distinguish between unicellular and multicellular organisms.
introduction: All living things, from the smallest bacteria to the largest blue whale, are made of cells. The cell is the basic unit of life. While all cells share some common parts, plants and animals have specific differences that allow them to survive in different ways.
content:
1. Common Organelles

Both plant and animal cells contain these essential parts:

  • Cell Membrane: The 'gatekeeper' that controls what enters and leaves the cell.
  • Nucleus: The 'control center' containing the cell's DNA.
  • Cytoplasm: The jelly-like substance where all organelles are suspended.
  • Mitochondria: The 'powerhouse' that produces energy through cellular respiration.
  • Vacuoles: Storage sacs for food, water, or waste.

2. Key Differences

Plants have two unique structures that animals do not:

  • Cell Wall: A rigid outer layer that provides support and protection.
  • Chloroplasts: Green organelles that capture sunlight to make food through Photosynthesis.

Conversely, animal cells usually have smaller, temporary vacuoles and contain Centrioles which help in cell division.

3. Unicellular vs. Multicellular

  • Unicellular: Organisms made of only one cell (e.g., Bacteria, Amoeba).
  • Multicellular: Organisms made of many specialized cells (e.g., Humans, Mango trees).

examples.title: Onion Skin Cells (Plant)
examples.description: Under a microscope, onion cells look like rectangular bricks because of the rigid cell wall.

examples.title: Cheek Cells (Animal)
examples.description: Human cheek cells appear irregular and rounded because they lack a cell wall.

keyTerms.definition: A specialized subunit within a cell that has a specific function.
The process by which plants make their own food.
The genetic material that carries instructions for life.

keyConcepts: Cells are the basic structural and functional units of all organisms.
Plant cells are autotrophic (make food), while animal cells are heterotrophic (consume food).
Multicellularity allows for higher complexity and specialization of tissues.
summary: While plant and animal cells share organelles like the nucleus and mitochondria, plants are distinguished by their cell walls and chloroplasts. Understanding these structures helps us understand how life functions at its most basic level.

selfCheck.q: Which organelle is known as the 'powerhouse' of the cell?
What two parts are present in plant cells but absent in animal cells?
Is a human being a unicellular or multicellular organism?
